quarterly_data.quarter: Stella Chemifa annual securities report: FY2026 (06-18-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Fiscal year ended March 31, 2026 (annual securities report): net sales JPY 36,799 million (+1.4%), operating income JPY 4,644 million (+7.1%), ordinary income JPY 4,424 million (+6.3%), profit attributable to owners of the parent JPY 3,058 million (+5.7%). Transportation segment: net sales JPY 4,892 million (+5.5%), operating income JPY 1,045 million (+31.6%).

quarterly_data.quarter: Stella Chemifa annual securities report: FY2026 (06-18-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: The 4th Medium-Term Management Plan (fiscal years ending March 2026 to March 2028) targets operating income of JPY 5.5 billion and ROE of 8.0% or more in the fiscal year ending March 2028, driven by growth of the High-Purity Chemicals business; the company states that FY ended March 2026 net sales, operating income and ROE all exceeded the prior year. Separately, it aims to create new businesses of JPY 5 billion to 10 billion in scale by the mid-2030s from fluorine-chemistry R&D (new semiconductor chemicals for customer needs, cell culture vessels, inorganic fluoride nanoparticles, and a flow synthesis method incorporating its fluorine technology).
quarterly_data.figure: FYE March 2028 targets: operating income JPY 5.5 billion; ROE 8.0% or more

quarterly_data.quarter: Stella Chemifa annual securities report: FY2026 (06-18-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management priorities: with domestic and overseas semiconductor makers announcing investment plans, the company aims to expand sales of high-purity chemicals for semiconductors in line with customer needs and to grow its overseas share, in particular by approaching the North American and Taiwanese markets; it is working to further diversify suppliers of its key raw material, anhydrous hydrofluoric acid, which it sources mainly from China. Anhydrous hydrofluoric acid prices rose in FY ended March 2026 on higher Chinese market prices, and the company states it is passing raw material increases through to selling prices to minimise the profit impact. Improvement of its highly selective etching solution was completed at the end of 2025, with development and customer evaluation continuing. It also targets wider use of fluorides for communications applications, and, because enriched boric acid for nuclear facilities currently sells mainly to China, aims to expand those sales in Japan, Europe and North America.

quarterly_data.quarter: Stella Chemifa annual securities report: FY2026 (06-18-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Capital expenditure in the fiscal year ended March 2026 was JPY 4,235 million (including intangibles), centred on the Semiconductors division: JPY 4,006 million in High-Purity Chemicals, mainly to upgrade ultra-high-purity hydrofluoric acid production equipment, and JPY 226 million in Transportation. Planned: renewal and consolidation of the small and medium container filling equipment for semiconductor high-purity chemicals at the Sanpo Plant (Sakai), total JPY 6,220 million of which JPY 3,445 million paid, started January 2023; completion has been postponed by defective building construction work and is now scheduled for September 2027. The company states the new equipment will roughly double filling capacity while halving operating time.
quarterly_data.figure: FY capex JPY 4,235 million; Sanpo filling equipment JPY 6,220 million, completion September 2027

quarterly_data.quarter: Stella Chemifa annual securities report: FY2026 (06-18-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: R&D expenses in the fiscal year ended March 2026 were JPY 626 million, with 34 research staff (about 5% of employees). Themes centre on chemicals for high-performance semiconductor manufacturing, high-definition display materials and materials for lithium-ion batteries: anti-reflection display materials using fluoride nanoparticle technology, dental materials, high-performance cell culture vessels using fluorination, cathode coating materials for liquid and all-solid-state lithium-ion batteries, LED phosphors and phosphor materials to improve the colour rendering of mini-LEDs, neutron shielding materials, and organic fluorine compound synthesis.
quarterly_data.figure: R&D expenses JPY 626 million; 34 R&D staff
